question: Why are Southeast claims taking longer to close since May 2026?

report.interpretation: Cycle time is the median days from report date to close date for closed Southeast claims (FL, GA, NC), grouped by report month. This is the agreed cycle_time_days definition. I compared Jan-Apr 2026 with May-Jul 2026. I left out Aug-Sep because those months still have many open claims, so their cycle times look artificially short.
report.answer: The slowdown is real and specific to the Southeast. Median time to close rose from 28 days (Jan-Apr reports) to 38 days (May-Jul reports). It peaked at 40 days for July reports. Other regions were flat: California 25.5 to 28, North 27 to 28, Texas 27 to 24. The best-supported cause is lost adjuster capacity. Southeast adjusters ADJ-016 and ADJ-017 left on 2026-05-01 and 2026-05-15. They had handled about 40% of closed Southeast claims (459 of 1,453), with medians of 24-26 days. Since then the four remaining adjusters handle all new claims, and each one's median rose from about 25-26 days to 31-34 days. The slowdown appears across nearly all causes, so it isn't a mix shift. Examples: collision 23 to 31 days, water damage 37 to 54, and glass 6 to 10.5. The share of bodily injury and liability claims was stable at about 8-11%. The adjuster link is a correlation in timing. The data has no workload or staffing-level field to confirm it directly. The apparent improvement in Aug-Sep is an artifact of open claims: 62 of August's 143 reports and 114 of September's 135 are still open.
report.answer_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN report_date<'2026-05-01' THEN 'Jan-Apr 2026' ELSE 'May-Jul 2026' END AS period, count(*) AS closed_claims, median(date_diff('day',report_date,close_date)) AS median_days_to_close FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND status='closed' AND report_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC

findings.claim: Southeast median cycle time rose about 10 days after April, while other regions were flat or improved.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT region, median(date_diff('day',report_date,close_date)) FILTER (WHERE report_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-04-30') pre, median(date_diff('day',report_date,close_date)) FILTER (WHERE report_date BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-07-31') post FROM claims WHERE status='closed' GROUP BY 1

findings.claim: Two of the six Southeast adjusters left in May (ADJ-016 on 05-01, ADJ-017 on 05-15). Every remaining adjuster's median time to close rose.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT a.adjuster_id, a.leave_date, count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.report_date>='2026-05-01') n_may, median(date_diff('day',c.report_date,c.close_date)) FILTER (WHERE c.report_date>='2026-05-01') med_may, median(date_diff('day',c.report_date,c.close_date)) FILTER (WHERE c.report_date<'2026-05-01') med_pre FROM claims c JOIN adjusters a USING(adjuster_id) WHERE c.region='Southeast' AND c.status='closed' GROUP BY ALL

findings.claim: The slowdown is broad across causes, so it is not driven by more complex bodily injury or liability claims.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT cause, median(date_diff('day',report_date,close_date)) FILTER (WHERE report_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-04-30') med_pre, median(date_diff('day',report_date,close_date)) FILTER (WHERE report_date BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-07-31') med_post FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND status='closed' GROUP BY 1

hypotheses.hypothesis: Loss of two Southeast adjusters reduced capacity
hypotheses.evidence: Both left in May, and the four remaining adjusters all slowed. There is no staffing or workload field, so this is circumstantial.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shift in mix toward slower causes (bodily injury/liability)
hypotheses.evidence: The share of bodily injury and liability claims was stable at about 8-11%, and most causes slowed individually.
California, North and Texas medians were flat or lower.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Data artifact from incomplete recent months
hypotheses.evidence: The comparison uses Jan-Jul reports only, where nearly all claims are closed. Aug-Sep look faster only because their slow claims are still open.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spike in claim volume (for example a weather event)
hypotheses.evidence: Southeast reports were steady at about 100-108 per month from May to July. They rose to 143 in August, which is after the slowdown began. I did not check weather events in detail.

data_quality_issues.issue: Aug-Sep 2026 report months are immature: many claims are still open, and only closed claims count in cycle time.
data_quality_issues.impact: Recent cycle times look falsely fast, so those months were excluded.

proposed_actions.title: Review Southeast adjuster staffing and backfill ADJ-016/ADJ-017
proposed_actions.reason: Cycle time has risen about 10 days since two adjusters left in May, and August report volume rose to 143 claims, up from about 100-108 a month.

open_questions: Were the departed adjusters replaced, and when? The warehouse has no staffing-level data.
